intro: Postal clerks serve the public, handle money and follow detailed procedures, skills that postal management and clerical jobs use. The closest of the 25 careers below is Postmasters and Mail Superintendents, with an 82% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $96,660, which is 56% more than the $62,130 postal clerks earn.
why_it_works: A window shift means helping a long line of customers, weighing and pricing mail and balancing cash at the end of the day. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job, and social perceptiveness and time management at 3. Postal management, order processing and title work use the same skills. Most other clerical matches pay less. The gaps are teaching and supervising.
tips: Apply for supervisor and postmaster openings inside the Postal Service; it is the clearest raise.
Gambling Managers earn $93,220, which is 50% more, and value cash handling and service.
Auto damage insurance appraisers earn $78,240, or 26% more, after a certificate.

faq.q: What jobs can former postal clerks do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Postmasters and Mail Superintendents (82%), Order Clerks (78%) and Procurement Clerks (76%), based on O*NET 31.0. Title examiners are 75% matched and earn $58,650, which is 6% less than the $62,130 postal clerk median.

faq.q: Which careers for postal clerks pay more?
faq.a: 8 of the 25 matches pay more. Postmasters earn $96,660 (56% more), Gambling Managers $93,220 (50% more) and auto damage insurance appraisers $78,240 (26% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most office clerk jobs pay less than postal work.

faq.q: Do postal clerks need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than postal clerks already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 62% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and the Postal Service promotes many supervisors from within.

faq.q: What skills should postal clerks learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, managing people, coordination and negotiation. Judgment already rates 2.88 out of 5 for postal clerks in O*NET, so training coworkers and supervising a shift are the main steps toward postal management.
